title: Converging legacy function surface with OpenAI-style tool calls: call policy and signature reconciliation
creator: Aisha Martinez
description:
Summary:
We need a coherent runtime and API behavior that allows Redwood customers to migrate from legacy 'function' invocation surfaces to OpenAI-style 'tool' calls without breaking production traffic. This ticket scopes the engineering work to create a compatibility layer that: (1) maps legacy function signatures to tool metadata, (2) reconciles differences in streaming semantics and partial results, (3) provides a deterministic fallback policy for mismatched names/params, and (4) provides a staged rollout path with clear telemetry and QA gates.

Why this matters:
- Many customers have workloads wired to the older 'function' payload shape (name, args JSON, callback_url patterns). Newer integrations (and partner ecosystems) expect OpenAI-style tool descriptors (description, parameters JSON Schema, required fields). Without a careful compatibility plan we risk customer outages, silent failures when a model selects the tool, and mismatched billing/latency characteristics.

Success criteria:
- Runtime exposes a per-customer compatibility mode that can be toggled per-route (default: permissive passthrough with opt-in strictness).
- >=95% of existing legacy function calls are successfully translated to tool calls in Canary tests with no semantic regressions.
- Streaming behavior: partial content and tool-invocation markers are preserved across both surfaces.
- Rollout telemetry for mismatches (name, param coercion, JSON schema errors) emitted with tags: route, customer_tier, model_family, compat_mode.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Surface mapping table: build a lightweight mapping resource (in-memory, persisted in configstore) that links legacy function identifiers to tool descriptors. This mapping supports: synonyms, deprecated_aliases, and a confidence score.
2) Signature reconciliation engine: when a request arrives that will invoke a tool/function, the runtime will attempt an ordered reconciliation: exact match by name -> alias match -> signature-based fuzzy match (param keys & types) -> fallback policy. Rules are deterministic and logged.
3) Param coercion & validation: use the tool parameters JSON Schema when present; for legacy functions, derive a best-effort schema based on historical payload examples and type hints recorded in the mapping table. Coercion rules are pluggable and opt-out per customer.
4) Streaming compatibility: define a small set of streaming events that represent tool lifecycle (tool_call_start, tool_stdout_chunk, tool_call_end, tool_error). Ensure both legacy and OpenAI-style paths emit these events and that the API proxy translates between event protocols.
5) Runtime perf: ensure the mapping & reconciliation adds <1ms median overhead in the fast path; detailed telemetry for tail latency during canaries.
6) Rollout plan: unit tests -> integration tests with synthetic workloads -> internal canary (small subset of traffic) -> invited customers -> full rollout.

Trade-offs & open questions:
- State vs. stateless mapping: keeping mappings in-memory improves latency but complicates multi-region config sync. Proposal: primary configstore in control plane + per-region cache with 30s TTL and invalidation hooks.
- Fuzzy matching sensitivity: tight thresholds reduce accidental matches but increase the number of calls that hit fallback. We'll configure thresholds conservatively and expose tuning flags per-customer.
- Telemetry volume: emitting detailed param-coercion traces will increase storage. We'll sample high-cardinality traces and emit counters/histograms for all events.

Implementation plan & tasks (engineering):
- ENG-50277.1: mapping service prototype (control-plane CRUD + per-region cache).
- ENG-50277.2: reconciliation module in runtime (match logic + deterministic fallback).
- ENG-50277.3: streaming event contract & translation layer tests.
- ENG-50277.4: parameter schema inference script + migration utility to pre-populate mappings using historical payload logs.
- ENG-50277.5: e2e test harness + canary orchestration playbook.

Testing & QA:
- Create synthetic corpus reflecting 10k historical legacy function calls (varying shapes) and validate translation correctness.
- Contract tests between runtime and console (mapping UI + edit flows).
- Load tests to measure added latency and tail risk under heavy batching.

Monitoring & Alerts:
- New dashboards: compat-matches-by-route, param-coercion-failures, fuzzy-match-rate, mapping-cache-staleness.
- Alerts: fuzzy-match-rate spike (>1% sustained), param-validation-errors (>0.1% for production routes), mapping-cache-misses >5% of requests.

Docs & customer communication:
- Update migration guide (Confluence) with examples for common patterns and recommended compat_mode settings.
- Publish a short changelog note for customers who use legacy functions with examples on how to opt into strict validation.

Links & artifacts:
- Migration design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CORE/Legacy+Fn+to+Tool+Convergence
- Draft PR (runtime): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4318
- Mapping UI mock: https://drive.redwood.ai/file/d/1abcMappingMock/edit
- Canary playbook: https://docs.redwood.ai/playbooks/tool-compat-canary.md

Risks:
- Silent schema coercion could change downstream behavior (high customer impact for billing/fulfillment flows). Mitigation: default to non-coercive mode for high-impact customers and require an explicit opt-in.
- Edge cases where streaming intermediary (third-party tool) expects callbacks in the legacy format. Mitigation: maintain a thin compatibility proxy for callback translation and include in canary tests.

Next immediate steps (this sprint):
- Spike: implement reconciliation module prototype and run against a 10k-sample dataset (owner: Liam).
- Control-plane schema: define mapping resource and CRUD API (owner: Priya Singh).
- Draft telemetry schema and Kibana dashboards (owner: DataInfra team contact: Marco Liu).
